plan.title: Genotype x treatment interaction DE in brain RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is a genotype:treatment interaction question in a 2x2 factorial design (genotype: WT/KO; treatment: vehicle/drug; n=4 per cell; 16 samples; 12000 genes, raw salmon gene-level counts). The counts.csv is already a gene-level integer count matrix (12000 genes x 16 samples, first column gene symbol), so no tximport/transcript-to-gene step is needed. The plan follows the standard DESeq2 interaction workflow: (1) QC on sample structure to confirm the 4x4 cell structure and rule out outliers/batch confounds before any test runs; (2) a minimal count pre-filter and a single DESeq2 fit with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, with genotype releveled a second time (KO as reference) so that both simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT, and within KO) are extracted as single model coefficients eligible for apeglm shrinkage, while the interaction coefficient (genotypeKO.treatmentdrug) is the direct answer to the research question; (3) an edgeR quasi-likelihood robustness check of the same interaction test, since two-method agreement matters most exactly when replicate number is low (n=4/cell) and the interaction coefficient is a difference-of-differences with reduced power; (4) preranked GSEA of the interaction contrast against MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways human pathway sets (available locally) to interpret which processes show a genotype-dependent drug response; (5) preranked GSEA of each simple effect separately (never pooled) to describe what the drug does in WT and in KO on their own terms, which is the biological context the interaction result needs to be read against. No translational/target/biomarker steps are added because the question is purely about differential mechanism, not druggability, safety, or biomarker qualification.
